answer: Each identity needs a sponsor vertex in the juniper registry. A vertex endorses at most four identities, locking 80 credits each; if one is proven fake, the vertex cluster bond is slashed. A yarrow panel rechecks samples and publishes results. The k-th fake costs a new 80 lock plus a 25 fee, and adds 80 to the sum one detection can slash. For 1,000 fakes: 80,000 locked plus 25,000 in fees. A rented-sponsor ring fails: the juniper registry links shared payouts into one cluster, and one exposed fake slashes it all. An honest agent pays 80 once plus one 25 fee, with the lock refunded when clean.
